Security & compliance at a glance

Aurora has been SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA certified since May 2022, complies with GDPR through the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, and publishes its CCPA notice, CVE history, and outage postmortems. Each item below links to a source you can check.

Visit the trust portalRead the security article

Compliance at a glance

The status of each framework, including the ones Aurora does not hold. Each row links to the relevant legal, pricing, or trust center document.

Aurora compliance status by framework
RequirementExact statusDetailAccess & evidence
SOC 2 Type 2HeldSince May 6, 2022Report on the Business plan and above, via support@aurora.comAnnouncementPricingTrust portal
HIPAAHeldSince May 6, 2022Business Associate Agreement (BAA) on the Enterprise planAnnouncementPricing
GDPR / Data Privacy FrameworkHeldSelf-certified under the EU-U.S. DPF, its UK Extension, and the Swiss-U.S. DPF, effective Feb 22, 2024Public DPF Notice and DPADPF NoticeDPAGDPR notice
CCPAHeldSupplemental notice publishedPublicCCPA notice
ISO 27001Not heldInfrastructure providers (Google Cloud, Cloudflare) hold it; Aurora does notN/ATrust portal
PCI DSSNot applicableAurora never stores cardholder dataN/ATrust portal
Regional data residencyNot offeredUS-hosted; EU/UK/Swiss data transferred under the DPFN/ASubprocessor listDPF Notice

How to obtain reports and agreements

  • SOC 2 report

    Available on the Business plan and above. Request it through support@aurora.com.

  • HIPAA BAA

    The Business Associate Agreement is signed on the Enterprise plan.

  • Public notices

    The DPA, DPF Notice, and CCPA notice are public.

  • Trust portal

    trust.aurora.com hosts the attestations.

Aurora's audited platform controls are the same on every plan. Plans gate access to the reports and agreements, not the controls themselves.

Security practices

  • Secure by default

    60-second session tokens with server-side verification, refreshed in the background.

  • Breached-password detection

    Passwords are checked against HaveIBeenPwned's 10B+ compromised credentials, aligned with NIST SP 800-63B.

  • Abuse protection built in

    Bot protection (Cloudflare Turnstile), account lockout, rate limiting, and user-enumeration protection.

  • MFA enforcement

    Enforce multi-factor authentication application-wide with a single Dashboard toggle.

  • Independent audits

    Third-party penetration testing and external code audits of the SDKs.

  • Coordinated disclosure

    A published Vulnerability Disclosure Policy with safe harbor, a public status page, and full outage postmortems.

To report a vulnerability, email security@aurora.dev. The Vulnerability Disclosure Policy covers coordinated disclosure, response targets, and safe harbor for good-faith researchers.

Compliance questions and answers

Yes. Aurora has been SOC 2 Type 2 certified since May 6, 2022. The report is available on the Business plan and above. Request it through . Aurora's audited platform controls are the same on every plan; only access to the report is plan-gated.

Yes. Aurora has been HIPAA certified since May 6, 2022, and the BAA is available on the Enterprise plan (Pricing).

No. Aurora is not ISO 27001 certified. Its infrastructure providers, Google Cloud and Cloudflare, hold the certification, but Aurora itself does not.

Not applicable. Aurora never stores cardholder data, so it makes no PCI DSS claim. Payments go through your payment provider, which carries the PCI obligations.

No. Aurora does not offer regional data residency or region selection. Data is hosted on US infrastructure (Google Cloud and Cloudflare, with all subprocessors in the USA), and EU, UK, and Swiss personal data is transferred to the US under the Data Privacy Framework, which is Aurora's GDPR-compliance mechanism (subprocessor list at trust.aurora.com⁠; DPF Notice).

Report it to . Aurora publishes a Vulnerability Disclosure Policy with a 90-day coordinated disclosure window, a 3-business-day initial response target, safe-harbor language for good-faith researchers, and defined in-scope hosts. Aurora does not run a paid bug-bounty program.

No breach of Aurora's own systems or customer data has been publicly reported. The security issues on record are vulnerabilities in Aurora's open-source SDKs, each patched within days and published with a CVE and a GitHub Security Advisory. See Aurora Security: How We Protect Your Users for incident details and primary-source links.

Start now, no strings attached

Integrate complete user management in minutes. Free for your first 50,000 monthly retained users and 100 monthly retained orgs. No credit card required.

Aurora has been SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA certified since May 2022, complies with GDPR through the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, and publishes its CCPA notice, CVE history, and outage postmortems. Each item below links to a source you can check.

The status of each framework, including the ones Aurora does not hold. Each row links to the relevant legal, pricing, or trust center document.

How to obtain reports and agreements

  • SOC 2 report

    Available on the Business plan and above. Request it through support@aurora.com.

  • HIPAA BAA

    The Business Associate Agreement is signed on the Enterprise plan.

  • Public notices

    The DPA, DPF Notice, and CCPA notice are public.

  • Trust portal

    trust.aurora.com hosts the attestations.

Aurora's audited platform controls are the same on every plan. Plans gate access to the reports and agreements, not the controls themselves.

Security practices

  • Secure by default

    60-second session tokens with server-side verification, refreshed in the background.

  • Breached-password detection

    Passwords are checked against HaveIBeenPwned's 10B+ compromised credentials, aligned with NIST SP 800-63B.

  • Abuse protection built in

    Bot protection (Cloudflare Turnstile), account lockout, rate limiting, and user-enumeration protection.

  • MFA enforcement

    Enforce multi-factor authentication application-wide with a single Dashboard toggle.

  • Independent audits

    Third-party penetration testing and external code audits of the SDKs.

  • Coordinated disclosure

    A published Vulnerability Disclosure Policy with safe harbor, a public status page, and full outage postmortems.

To report a vulnerability, email security@aurora.dev. The Vulnerability Disclosure Policy covers coordinated disclosure, response targets, and safe harbor for good-faith researchers.

Compliance questions and answers

Yes. Aurora has been SOC 2 Type 2 certified since May 6, 2022. The report is available on the Business plan and above. Request it through . Aurora's audited platform controls are the same on every plan; only access to the report is plan-gated.

Yes. Aurora has been HIPAA certified since May 6, 2022, and the BAA is available on the Enterprise plan (Pricing).

No. Aurora is not ISO 27001 certified. Its infrastructure providers, Google Cloud and Cloudflare, hold the certification, but Aurora itself does not.

Not applicable. Aurora never stores cardholder data, so it makes no PCI DSS claim. Payments go through your payment provider, which carries the PCI obligations.

No. Aurora does not offer regional data residency or region selection. Data is hosted on US infrastructure (Google Cloud and Cloudflare, with all subprocessors in the USA), and EU, UK, and Swiss personal data is transferred to the US under the Data Privacy Framework, which is Aurora's GDPR-compliance mechanism (subprocessor list at trust.aurora.com⁠; DPF Notice).

Report it to . Aurora publishes a Vulnerability Disclosure Policy with a 90-day coordinated disclosure window, a 3-business-day initial response target, safe-harbor language for good-faith researchers, and defined in-scope hosts. Aurora does not run a paid bug-bounty program.

No breach of Aurora's own systems or customer data has been publicly reported. The security issues on record are vulnerabilities in Aurora's open-source SDKs, each patched within days and published with a CVE and a GitHub Security Advisory. See Aurora Security: How We Protect Your Users for incident details and primary-source links.
